text: The prophet Ezra saw God's angel. He questioned him one matter at a time, and the angel came near and told him what would take place at the end.
The angel said: For the righteous there are light, rest, and everlasting life; for sinners, punishment without end.
Ezra said: If this is so, then fortunate are the beasts of the earth, the creeping things, and the birds of heaven, for they do not wait for resurrection and judgment.
The angel answered: You do wrong to say this. God made all things for humankind, and humankind for God; each person is judged by the state in which God finds that person.
Ezra asked: When you take the souls of human beings, where do you lead them?
The angel said: I lead the souls of the righteous to worship God and set them in the upper air; demons seize the souls of sinners and keep them confined in the air.
Ezra asked: And the soul caught in Satan's grasp, when will it be released?
The angel said: If someone in this world remembers that soul for good, prayer and mercy can rescue it from Satan.
Ezra asked: By what means? The angel answered: By prayers, acts of mercy, and offerings.
Ezra asked: If the sinful soul has no good remembrance to help it, what will become of that soul?
The angel said: Such a soul remains in Satan's grasp until Christ comes. When Gabriel's trumpet sounds,
then the souls are freed from Satan's grasp and descend through the air.
They come and are joined again to their respective bodies, now turned to dust; the trumpet's call fashions them, raises them, and renews them.
Christ our God lifts them up to meet him as he comes to judge the earth—the righteous and the sinners—and to repay each according to that person's deeds.
